title: Nested loop makes orders_for_users O(users * orders) instead of O(users + orders)
body: For every user, the inner loop scans the entire orders list to find matches (lines 5-9). For U users and O orders this costs O(U*O) comparisons instead of O(U+O). Build an index once by grouping orders by user_id (e.g. a defaultdict(list) populated in a single pass over orders), then look up each user's matches in O(1) amortized. This is a warm-path aggregation helper (report generation) that will be run repeatedly over the full users/orders sets, so the quadratic blowup will be felt as latency growth as either collection grows, without falling over outright.
